clue.text: Let Local Education Authorities take note

parts.note: LEAs is the abbreviation for Local Education Authorities, the old English council education bodies
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Council education departments are told to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to rent it out under a contract, so the noun-turned-verb sense is a synonym.

clue.text: Gaunt house of ancestral design

indicators.note: of ancestral design suggests the letters of ancestral are laid out to a new plan

explanation.surface: A lean old family home with an inherited look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaunt' looks like thin; it is John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, founder of the royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: John of Gaunt, son of Edward III, founded the royal dynasty that bears this ducal name.

clue.text: A pitiful and indifferent result

parts.note: pitiful and pathetic both mean arousing pity or contempt

explanation.surface: A poor, lacklustre outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking interest or concern is being indifferent.

clue.text: Cheese is over-produced

indicators.note: over in a down clue tells us the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: produced means made

explanation.surface: Too much cheese is being made.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax rind is one kind of cheese.

clue.text: Lack of employment in the lean years

parts.note: lean and spare both mean thin, with no excess flesh
years can stand for time, as in 'in years past'

explanation.surface: Unemployment was common during the hard, thin years.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure hours are those free of work, so a lack of employment is what fills them.

clue.text: Wild stab made by the nocturnal gunman

definitions.meaning: a firearm discharged at night, aimed blind

explanation.surface: A gunman firing at night is guessing at his target.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind guess is a wild stab, and a gunman at night fires literally without seeing.

clue.text: English archdeacon is cool and collected

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: An English church official stays calm.
explanation.definitionFit: An even temper is one that is calm and composed.

clue.text: won't be placed under another's influence

indicators.note: be placed suggests the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be dominated by another person.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the opening 'I'; the anagram of I and WONT gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being led along by someone else means being under their sway.

clue.text: Previous part of the play, to be precise

parts.note: ex means former or previous, as in ex-husband
an act is a main division of a play

explanation.surface: An earlier section of a drama, to be accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exact means being precise and correct.

clue.text: The creature found in many a land

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An animal that lives in numerous countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Short race organised by an association of players

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters of the two words are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A brief running event is put on by a sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like athletes after 'race', but here they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphonic band is a body of musicians playing together.

clue.text: The latest news from Henley Regatta

definitions.meaning: Henley Royal Regatta is a rowing meeting on the Thames, so its races are contests on moving water

explanation.surface: The newest reports come in from a rowing regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley Royal Regatta is a famous English rowing event on the River Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical news is about what is happening now, and the regatta's races take place on a flowing river.

clue.text: Bill, the man is a pain

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a certain fellow named Bill is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent hurt is a pain.

clue.text: Record of dairy manufacture

indicators.note: manufacture suggests the word dairy is made over into something new

explanation.surface: A log of milk production at a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily journal is a written record of events.

clue.text: Bring back the strap in Scotland and use it

indicators.note: bring back tells us to take the word for the strap and read it the other way

parts.note: the taws is a leather strap formerly used for punishment in Scottish schools

explanation.surface: A call to restore corporal punishment in Scottish schools and apply it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' sounds like restoring the punishment, but it reverses TAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike with a strap is to hit with a sharp blow, as one does a fly.

clue.text: What trained detectives need to solve a second murder

parts.note: to murder is to kill

explanation.surface: Investigators need expertise to crack a further killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise gained through training is ability or skill.

clue.text: Formermonk

definitions.meaning: the head of a religious house, below an abbot

explanation.surface: A man who used to be in holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is earlier in time; the other is a monastic superior ranking below an abbot.

clue.text: Draw out money and get acknowledgement

definitions.meaning: to take sums lent on account at a bank
to accept the praise for something done

explanation.surface: A man withdraws a loan and gets thanked for it.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is drawing on a bank loan, the other is claiming the praise for an achievement.

clue.text: Belief in God contains a flaw-and it's absolute

definitions.note: absolute here is shorthand for absolute rule, a noun sense

indicators.note: contains says the word for belief holds the flaw inside it

parts.note: deism is belief in a creator God
a spot is a blemish or flaw

explanation.surface: A theologian says faith has a defect, and it is total.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannical one-man rule is absolutism, the unchecked power of an autocrat.

clue.text: Time to arrange a reading of his drama

definitions.text: Time to arrange a reading of his drama

indicators.note: arrange suggests the letters of a reading are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright decides it is time to organise a read-through of his play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragic actor or playwright would hold a read-through of his play.

clue.text: The reminiscences of groups of sappers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British army's sappers
collections are groups of things gathered together

explanation.surface: An old soldier recalls tales of army engineer units.
explanation.walkthrough: The groups come first in the clue but follow RE in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Memories of the past are reminiscences.

clue.text: Anglicans take it to heart, for instance

indicators.note: taking something to heart puts it in the middle of the word for the church

parts.note: CE, the Church of England, stands for Anglicans

explanation.surface: Churchgoers take a remark seriously, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote as an example is to give something for instance.

clue.text: Angry symbol of the Church militant

definitions.meaning: the emblem carried by Christians, as in 'Onward Christian soldiers'

explanation.surface: An angry emblem of a fighting church.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is annoyed; the other is the Christian emblem borne by the Church militant.

clue.text: The cloth costing a pretty penny once

parts.note: twee means pretty in an over-dainty way
D was the abbreviation for the old pre-decimal penny

explanation.surface: Fabric that used to cost a fair sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pretty penny' reads as a large sum; split it. The old British penny was written d.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen fabric from Scotland is a cloth.

clue.text: Green finds one in the main body of the church

indicators.note: in places the letter for one within the church part

parts.words: the main body of the church
parts.note: the nave is the central part of a church where the congregation sits
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An environmentalist discovers someone sitting in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour or an environmentalist; it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A green beginner is inexperienced and unworldly.

clue.text: Devotion counts for nothing

definitions.meaning: in tennis scoring this word means a score of zero

explanation.surface: A cynic says that faithfulness gets you nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is deep affection; the other is the tennis term for a zero score.

clue.text: Raise objections to a cigarette-end

indicators.note: raise in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a discarded cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: The burnt-down end of a cigarette is its stub.

clue.text: Fashionable young lady goes to a festival

indicators.note: goes to puts the young lady's word in front of the letter that follows

parts.note: a gal is a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish girl attends a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration.

clue.text: Surprised to learn that the bowler's been on

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bowler delivers a set of six balls; once he has bowled, that set has been taken

explanation.surface: A spectator is startled to hear that a particular bowler has already had his turn.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six balls by one bowler, so when he has been on, an over has been TAKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught out by events is to be surprised; the cricket reading splits the word into its two parts.

clue.text: Common excuse for getting a book, I conclude

indicators.note: conclude says the letter I comes at the end of the word

parts.note: LIB, short for Latin liber, is an abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone claims a library visit as the standard reason for being late.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that one was elsewhere is the classic excuse.

clue.text: The team is fired with longing to let its hair down!

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
someone who burns with desire is fired with longing

explanation.surface: A keen team cannot wait to relax and enjoy itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let its hair down' suggests partying; the definition is literal, hair grown down the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskers grown down the side of the face are hair allowed to run down.

clue.text: Capital affirmation of virility

definitions.meaning: the seat of government of a country
read as two words a man would say to declare himself male

explanation.surface: A city proclaims its manhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Jordan, and split in two it reads as a statement of being a man.
